briefs.title: empty review statistics contract testing
briefs.description: Use empty review statistics contract testing to verify an empty list, zero average, and zero total before a skill receives its first review.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you prove a skill with no reviews returns an empty list, averageRating zero, and totalReviews zero?

outline.heading: What Must Empty Review Statistics Contract Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define the exact JSON contract for a valid skill with no review rows and distinguish it from missing skillId and database failure responses.

outline.heading: What Should a No Reviews API Response Contain?
outline.coverage: Assert reviews is an array, averageRating is numeric zero, totalReviews is numeric zero, and no nullable aggregate leaks into JSON.

outline.heading: How Do You Build a Null AVG Fallback Test?
outline.coverage: Use PostgreSQL aggregate behavior on an empty input and verify the route converts null average and count output to stable numeric values.

outline.heading: Empty Review List Contract Across Query Outcomes
outline.coverage: Compare zero rows, rows hidden by the inner join, missing query input, and thrown database operations without treating them as one state.

outline.heading: How Do You Write a Zero Total Reviews Assertion?
outline.coverage: Check value and type so string zero, null, undefined, and stale nonzero counts fail with useful diagnostics.

outline.heading: First Review State Testing
outline.coverage: Add one review after the empty assertion and prove list length, count, and average move together from the zero state.

outline.heading: Empty-State Input and Response Matrix
outline.coverage: Present valid and invalid request cases with database fixtures, HTTP status, list shape, average, and total.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Empty-State Procedure?
outline.coverage: Create a skill without reviews, call GET, validate the JSON schema, add one review, and repeat to catch stale aggregates.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about PostgreSQL AVG, count, numeric JSON types, nonexistent skills, inner joins, and first-review transitions.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Reinforce the explicit empty-state contract and direct readers to the API-testing catalog.

procedurePlan.heading: How to verify empty review statistics
steps: Seed a skill and user without inserting any review rows.
Call GET with the seeded skill ID.
Assert a 200 response and the exact empty-list plus numeric-zero shape.
Query the database directly to prove the review table is empty.
Insert one review and call GET again.
Assert the list, average, and total transition consistently.

codeExamples.title: Assert the GET empty-state response
codeExamples.focus: Exercise the separate review and aggregate queries and verify their combined JSON output.

codeExamples.title: Seed a skill with no review rows
codeExamples.focus: Use the reviews schema to create an explicit empty fixture and then a first-review transition.

briefs.cta: Browse API testing skills at /skills and add the empty-review contract to your regression suite.

briefs.title: review rating boundary validation testing
briefs.description: Use review rating boundary validation testing to cover missing, fractional, string, and out-of-range values around the accepted one-to-five range.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test missing, null, fractional, string, zero, one, five, and six ratings against the review API?

outline.heading: What Must Review Rating Boundary Validation Testing Cover?
outline.coverage: Define the required field, integer requirement, inclusive one-to-five range, and the expected 400 response before database work.

outline.heading: How Do You Test Review API Rating Validation?
outline.coverage: Separate malformed JSON, missing rating, null rating, wrong types, and numeric range failures so every branch has a precise oracle.

outline.heading: What Belongs in an Integer Rating Boundary Test?
outline.coverage: Use boundary values zero, one, five, and six plus decimals, NaN-like JSON limitations, and large integers.

outline.heading: One to Five Rating QA Matrix
outline.coverage: Map valid values to 201 and invalid values to the exact validation message while confirming rejected requests create no row.

outline.heading: How Do You Prove Fractional Review Rating Rejection?
outline.coverage: Test representative decimals inside and outside the range and assert Number.isInteger blocks them before persistence.

outline.heading: Missing Rating Response Test Cases
outline.coverage: Contrast omitted, undefined before serialization, null, empty string, numeric string, boolean, and zero.

outline.heading: Rating Input, Status, Message, and Write Matrix
outline.coverage: Present the required table with body value, JavaScript type, accepted flag, status, error text, and database delta.

outline.heading: How Do You Implement Boundary Tests Without Partial Writes?
outline.coverage: Run the numbered POST procedure with authenticated fixtures and verify row counts before and after every rejected case.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about inclusive boundaries, numeric strings, fractions, JSON limits, database constraints, and validation order.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Summarize the boundary matrix and send readers to verified API-testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test review rating boundaries
steps: Create an authenticated user and an existing skill fixture.
Record the initial review row count.
POST each invalid body and assert the exact 400 response.
Verify the row count is unchanged after every rejection.
POST ratings one through five using fresh user fixtures.
Assert each valid integer returns 201 and preserves the submitted value.

codeExamples.title: Table-drive the POST rating branches
codeExamples.focus: Cover required-field checks and Number.isInteger plus inclusive range validation.

codeExamples.title: Assert database write boundaries
codeExamples.focus: Verify rejected ratings never reach the non-null integer column and accepted ratings persist unchanged.

briefs.cta: Browse API validation skills at /skills and reuse this boundary matrix for rating endpoints.

briefs.title: Postgres cascade delete relation testing
briefs.description: Use Postgres cascade delete relation testing to prove deleting a skill removes junction rows, installs, reviews, and pack items without orphans.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you prove deleting a skill removes its junction rows, installs, reviews, and pack items without leaving orphans?

outline.heading: What Must Postgres Cascade Delete Relation Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define the skill as the parent row and inventory every direct child relation whose foreign key declares onDelete cascade.

outline.heading: How Do You Write a Drizzle onDelete Cascade Test?
outline.coverage: Build a complete fixture graph, delete only the parent skill, and query every child table without manually deleting dependencies.

outline.heading: What Proves Postgres Orphan Row Prevention?
outline.coverage: Assert zero child rows by skill ID and test that a new child cannot reference the deleted parent.

outline.heading: Foreign Key Cascade Integration Test Scope
outline.coverage: Explain why a real PostgreSQL database is required and which assertions a schema-only unit test cannot establish.

outline.heading: How Do You Protect Skill Deletion Data Integrity?
outline.coverage: Verify unrelated skills, users, categories, and packs survive while only relationships owned by the deleted skill disappear.

outline.heading: Cascade Delete Multiple Relations Fixture Design
outline.coverage: Create category links, agent compatibility, installs, reviews, and pack items for one target and one control skill.

outline.heading: Relation, Foreign Key, and Expected Deletion Matrix
outline.coverage: Present every relation with its foreign key, cascade declaration, target-row outcome, and control-row outcome.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Full Cascade Procedure?
outline.coverage: Follow an ordered transaction-safe setup, deletion, orphan check, control check, and cleanup workflow.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about database versus ORM cascades, composite keys, nullable pack authors, transactions, controls, and migration drift.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Summarize the graph-level assertion and point to database testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to verify all skill cascades
steps: Create target and control skills plus shared supporting users, categories, and packs.
Insert one or more child rows in every skill-owned relation for both skills.
Record child counts grouped by target and control skill IDs.
Delete only the target skill in PostgreSQL.
Assert every target child count is zero and every control count is unchanged.
Attempt an orphan insert and assert the foreign key rejects it.

codeExamples.title: Build the complete relation fixture graph
codeExamples.focus: Insert rows for every cascading skill foreign key, including composite junction tables.

codeExamples.title: Delete the parent and assert control isolation
codeExamples.focus: Delete one skill ID and compare target and control child counts in a real database.

briefs.cta: Browse database testing skills at /skills and add a complete cascade fixture to your integration suite.

briefs.title: Typesense collection schema drift testing
briefs.description: Use Typesense collection schema drift testing to catch field-type, facet-flag, and default-sort differences before indexed documents fail in CI.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you catch field type, facet flag, and default sorting drift between the declared skills schema and indexed documents?

outline.heading: What Must Typesense Collection Schema Drift Testing Catch?
outline.coverage: Define drift across names, types, array shapes, facet flags, required fields, and default sorting assumptions.

outline.heading: How Do You Build a Typesense Schema Contract Test?
outline.coverage: Fetch or fixture the live collection schema and compare a normalized representation with skillsSchema in source.

outline.heading: What Does Facet Flag Drift Detection Verify?
outline.coverage: Assert every field used in filter_by or facet_by is declared with compatible type and facet behavior.

outline.heading: Search Document Type Mismatch Cases
outline.coverage: Cover scalar versus array values, int32 overflow risk, bool strings, timestamp units, and omitted fields.

outline.heading: How Do You Check the Typesense Default Sort Schema?
outline.coverage: Verify installCount exists with a sortable numeric type and matches the declared default_sorting_field exactly.

outline.heading: Collection Migration Regression Test Strategy
outline.coverage: Describe additive, breaking, and reindex-required changes and the assertions needed before switching collection aliases.

outline.heading: Declared Fields, Runtime Use, and Drift Impact
outline.coverage: Present the required field-by-field table linking schema declarations to query, facet, sort, and result-mapping use.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Drift Audit in CI?
outline.coverage: Normalize schemas, compare deterministic JSON, index representative documents, run one search, and fail with targeted differences.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about schema updates, collection aliases, optional fields, facet flags, int32 versus int64, and reindexing.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Summarize the contract boundary and direct readers to search-testing skills.

tablePlan.title: Typesense schema declaration and runtime-use map

procedurePlan.heading: How to detect collection schema drift
steps: Serialize the repository skillsSchema into a normalized field map.
Retrieve or fixture the deployed Typesense collection schema.
Compare field names, types, facet flags, and default sorting field.
Index one representative document containing every declared field.
Run the production query_by, facet_by, filter_by, and sort_by combinations.
Report structural differences separately from document indexing failures.

codeExamples.title: Normalize the declared skills collection schema
codeExamples.focus: Convert skillsSchema fields and default sorting field into a deterministic contract snapshot.

codeExamples.title: Trace every queried and mapped field
codeExamples.focus: Assert query_by, facet_by, filters, sorting, and SkillSummary mapping are represented in the schema.

briefs.cta: Browse search QA skills at /skills and run the schema drift audit before the next reindex.

briefs.title: install telemetry country header testing
briefs.description: Use install telemetry country header testing to verify cf-ipcountry extraction, missing defaults, unusual values, and persisted install data.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test cf-ipcountry extraction, missing-header defaults, unusual values, and persistence in install rows?

outline.heading: What Must Install Telemetry Country Header Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define request-header extraction, empty-string fallback, text persistence, and the boundary between edge-provided data and application validation.

outline.heading: How Do You Write a cf-ipcountry Header Test?
outline.coverage: Construct NextRequest fixtures with present, absent, lowercase, and representative country values, then inspect the inserted row.

outline.heading: What Is the Install Country Default Value?
outline.coverage: Show that the route supplies an empty string and the schema also declares an empty default, then test the route value explicitly.

outline.heading: Edge Geolocation Header Persistence Cases
outline.coverage: Cover two-letter values, Cloudflare special values, whitespace, long text, mixed case, and repeated requests without asserting geographic truth.

outline.heading: How Should Telemetry Country Validation Be Scoped?
outline.coverage: Distinguish the current pass-through behavior from a future allowlist and test what the code does today.

outline.heading: Missing Country Header QA
outline.coverage: Verify no exception occurs, success remains true, and the stored country is the documented empty string.

outline.heading: Header Input and Stored Country Matrix
outline.coverage: Present request values, header presence, normalized storage, response, and risk notes.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Country Persistence Procedure?
outline.coverage: Seed a resolvable skill, send table-driven requests, query the newest install row, and clean up by test run.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about Cloudflare headers, local development, missing values, special codes, trust boundaries, and personal data handling.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Summarize the persistence contract and link to telemetry-related skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test country header persistence
steps: Seed one skill whose slug resolves through the telemetry route.
Prepare request cases for present, absent, empty, and unusual header values.
POST one add event per case with a unique agent marker.
Query the matching install row and assert the exact country text.
Assert the response remains successful for each accepted header shape.
Remove all test rows and restore counters after the suite.

codeExamples.focus: Construct header variants and assert the value passed into the install insert.

codeExamples.title: Verify the persisted text default
codeExamples.focus: Query the installs.country column for present and missing-header cases.
